sources.title: The Lipid Bilayer
sources.publisher: Garland Science; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
sources.version: Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition; NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK26871
sources.locator: Sections on bilayer assembly and dynamics: hydrophobic molecules forcing adjacent water into icelike cages at a free-energy cost minimised by clustering; lipids aggregating spontaneously with tails buried; a bilayer avoiding edges only by closing into a sealed compartment, and a tear creating a free edge the lipids rearrange away; about 5 x 10^6 lipids per square micrometre and 10^9 in a small animal cell; the section The Lipid Bilayer Is a Two-dimensional Fluid.
sources.license: Publisher copyright 2002; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the physical account of bilayer assembly and self-sealing, the lipid counts, the lateral and transbilayer diffusion rates, the phase transition and its dependence on chain length and unsaturation, cholesterol's two effects and its effect on permeability, and the distribution of phospholipid classes between the two leaflets. No wording, figure, table, dataset, or example was copied or adapted; the crypt framing, the unit conversion, the crossing-time arithmetic, the order-of-magnitude comparison, and every teaching task are this lesson's own.

sources.title: Membrane Proteins
sources.publisher: Garland Science; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
sources.version: Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition; NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK26878
sources.locator: Statements that protein is less than 25 per cent of the myelin membrane's mass, about 75 per cent of ATP-producing membranes and about 50 per cent of a typical plasma membrane; that certain plasma membrane enzymes and transport proteins are confined to the apical surface of epithelial cells while others are confined to the basal and lateral surfaces; and that this separation of protein and lipid is thought to be maintained at least in part by tight junctions.
sources.license: Publisher copyright 2002; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the protein mass fractions of three named membranes and the confinement of particular plasma-membrane proteins to the apical or to the basal and lateral surfaces of an epithelial cell, together with the attribution of that separation at least in part to tight junctions. No wording, figure, table, or example was copied or adapted.

sources.title: Supramolecular chemistry in lipid bilayer membranes
sources.locator: Statement that the thickness of the hydrophobic interior of the membrane is typically 3 to 3.5 nm depending on composition, with an overall membrane thickness of around 5 to 5.5 nm including the hydrophilic phosphate head groups.

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the overall thickness of a lipid bilayer membrane and the thickness of its water-avoiding interior, and to establish that the block's working figure of about 5 nm is an order of magnitude within a stated range rather than a constant. sources.publisher: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
sources.locator: Statements that the plasma membrane holds hundreds if not thousands of phospholipid species; that sterols are its most abundant lipid and can be up to 40 per cent of total lipid; that lipid tracers diffuse about four times faster in model membranes than in living-cell plasma membranes, tabulated as 5 to 15 against 0.5 to 4 micrometres squared per second; and that the fluid mosaic model dates from 1971 to 1972 while heterogeneity was seen in the 1960s.

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the sterol share and phospholipid diversity of the plasma membrane, the measured slowdown of lipid diffusion in living cells against model membranes, and the date and correct reading of the fluid mosaic model. sources.title: Flippases and scramblases in the plasma membrane
sources.locator: Statements that phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin sit primarily in the outer leaflet while phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine are restricted to the cytoplasmic side; that flippases are ATP-dependent translocases moving those two inward while scramblases move phospholipids bidirectionally without ATP; that disrupting an established asymmetry unaided takes a half-time of several days; and that exposed phosphatidylserine promotes clotting and marks apoptotic cells.

No wording, figure, table, or example was copied or adapted.

sources.title: Role of flippases, scramblases and transfer proteins in phosphatidylserine subcellular distribution

sources.title: A temperature-sensitive metabolic valve and a transcriptional feedback loop drive rapid homeoviscous adaptation in Escherichia coli
creators: Stefan P. H. van den Berg
sources.locator: Statements that homeoviscous adaptation maintains membranes at a fixed viscosity across growth temperatures; that organisms counteract temperature by varying the proportion of packing-disrupting lipids such as unsaturated or branched-chain fatty acids, or by varying acyl chain length; that the trait is broadly conserved across prokaryotes and multicellular organisms; and that an Escherichia coli fabF deletion grew severely poorly, recovering on supplementation.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the definition of homeoviscous adaptation, the compositional strategies organisms use to hold viscosity steady, the broad conservation of the trait, and the growth defect and rescue of a bacterial strain unable to make the required lipid. No wording, figure, table, dataset, or example was copied or adapted, and the lesson states plainly that this demonstration is bacterial.

sources.title: Modulation of the bilayer thickness of exocytic pathway membranes by membrane proteins rather than cholesterol
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
sources.locator: Phosphate-to-phosphate bilayer thicknesses measured by solution x-ray scattering on membranes purified from rat liver: endoplasmic reticulum 37.5 plus or minus 0.4 angstroms, Golgi 39.5 plus or minus 0.4, basolateral plasma membrane 35.6 plus or minus 0.6, apical plasma membrane 42.5 plus or minus 0.3; with cholesterol depletion changing thickness by at most 1 angstrom while protein removal changed it by 4 to 5, so protein modulates thickness.

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the four measured phosphate-to-phosphate thicknesses, the tissue and method they came from, and the finding that protein rather than cholesterol accounts for the differences. sources.title: Intestinal epithelial cell polarity defects in disease: lessons from microvillus inclusion disease
sources.locator: Statements that the apical and basolateral membranes of all intestinal epithelial cells are two biochemically and functionally distinct domains with different protein and lipid compositions; that the apical membrane faces the lumen and both forms a defensive barrier against pathogens and processes and takes up nutrients; that the basolateral membrane is crucial for interactions with adjacent cells and the basement membrane; and that the tight junction sits between them.
